33 A metal electrical conductor has a resistance of 5.6 kΩ. A potential difference (p.d.) of 9.0 V is
applied across its ends.
How many electrons pass a point in the conductor in one minute?
A
6.0 × 1020
B
1.0 × 1019
C
6.0 × 1017
D
1.0 × 1016

hints: First list what is given: $R = 5.6 \, \text{k}\Omega = 5600 \, \Omega$, $V = 9.0 \, \text{V}$ and time $t = 1$ minute $= 60 \, \text{s}$.
Connect current to charge: use $I = V/R$ for the metal conductor, then total charge past a point is $Q = It$.
Connect charge to electron count with $Q = ne$, using $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C}$, then rearrange to $n = Q/e$.
walkthrough: Convert the resistance to ohms: $R = 5.6 \, \text{k}\Omega = 5.6 \times 10^3 \, \Omega = 5600 \, \Omega$. Time is $t = 60 \, \text{s}$.
Calculate the current from Ohm's law: $I = V/R = 9.0/5600 \approx 1.61 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{A}$.
Calculate the charge passing in one minute: $Q = It \approx 1.61 \times 10^{-3} \times 60 \approx 9.64 \times 10^{-2} \, \text{C}$.
Calculate the number of electrons using elementary charge $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C}$: $n = Q/e \approx 9.64 \times 10^{-2} / 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \approx 6.0 \times 10^{17}$.
This matches $6.0 \times 10^{17}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Too large by factor 1000, from using $5.6 \, \Omega$ instead of $5.6 \, \text{k}\Omega = 5600 \, \Omega$ for the current.

B.explanation: Too large by factor 60, from using $t = 1 \, \text{s}$ instead of $t = 60 \, \text{s}$ when finding charge $Q = It$.

C.explanation: Gives $I = V/R \approx 1.6 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{A}$ and $n = It/e \approx 6.0 \times 10^{17}$ electrons in $60 \, \text{s}$.

D.explanation: Too small by factor 60, from dividing by 60 instead of multiplying by 60 s, equivalent to electrons per second divided by 60.
